conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. I understand you’ve been having belly pain. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s in my upper belly, right here. It started three days ago and goes into my back. I also threw up twice today and had diarrhea this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, chest pain, or trouble breathing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, none of that. But I felt lightheaded when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. We checked your labs and chest X-ray. No infection or lung issues. Your lipase is a bit high, but not high enough to suggest pancreatitis. We think this is related to your gastroparesis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Gastroparesis again? I stopped my erythromycin for my usual break. I’ve had pain like this before when I stop it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That’s likely what triggered it. We’re restarting erythromycin and giving you IV fluids. We also gave you some medicine for pain and nausea in the ER.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. Will I be here long?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We expect just a day. Once your pain settles and you can eat without vomiting, we’ll send you home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs look stable. Your red blood cell count is a bit lower, but not concerning. You’re doing well — no more vomiting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I feel much better. The pain is almost gone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll try getting you something light to eat soon. If you tolerate it, you can go home later today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Should I keep taking erythromycin? I don’t want to keep having these episodes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re restarting it three times a day. We’ll talk to your gastroenterologist about whether you need a different plan instead of stopping it regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well. You ate a full meal and no symptoms. Your abdomen is soft and not tender. We’re clearing you to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What should I do if the pain comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep taking your erythromycin as prescribed. Use your pain and nausea meds as needed. If pain worsens or you can’t keep fluids down, come back. Otherwise, follow up with your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other medicines — should I keep taking them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, especially your anxiety and depression meds. We continued them here. Take them as usual at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in before discharge. You’re still feeling well?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, no pain, no nausea. Ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. Remember to follow up with your doctors and take your erythromycin regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One more thing — I felt dizzy earlier. Was that serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That lightheadedness was likely from dehydration when you weren’t keeping food down. With fluids and treatment, it’s resolved. Just stay hydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks for explaining.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re all set. We’re discharging you now. Feel better, and take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.
